entities.summary: John Capgrave (c. 1390-1464) was an English historian and scholastic theologian whose chronicles of the Anglo-Saxon and Norman periods remain invaluable for understanding the history of medieval England. Born in Norfolk, England, Capgrave studied at the University of Cambridge and later became a monk at Peterborough Abbey. His most notable work, *The Chronicle of the First Hundred Years of King Edward I*, offers a detailed account of the reign of King Edward I and the impact of the Norman Conquest on English society. Capgrave's writings not only provide insight into the political and social dynamics of medieval England but also demonstrate his commitment to preserving the history of the English monarchy. The legacy of John Capgrave can be seen in the work of later historians and scholars, who continued to build upon his chronicles and expand our understanding of medieval England. Through his meticulous research and writing, Capgrave left a lasting impact on the field of medieval studies, cementing his place as one of the most important historians of his era.
